clue.text: But is it suitable wear for a square dance?

definitions.text: But is it suitable wear for a square dance?

parts.words: But is it suitable wear for a square dance?
parts.note: a ball is round, so a dress named for one teasingly seems wrong for a square dance

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether a formal evening dress suits a country square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke plays on 'ball' as a round object: the formal dress is named after a ball, which is round, not square.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal dress worn to a grand dance, named after that kind of event.

clue.text: Generous girl having two husbands?

parts.note: a generous portion is a big one
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A big-hearted woman turns out to have two husbands.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of being married to two people at once; the question mark admits a phrase stands for the noun.

clue.text: They're known mainly as insurers

parts.note: the famous London insurance market, whose name many also know from a high-street bank

explanation.surface: A plain statement about some firm best known for providing insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The London insurance market shares its name with a British bank, so 'mainly' hedges: the name is chiefly linked with insurance underwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: The London market is the world's best-known insurance underwriting institution.

clue.text: Makes a wish and does well in company

parts.note: to make money is to get it
to long is to wish for something

explanation.surface: Someone blows out candles making a wish, and is good company at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a wish' reads as one idiom, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being on friendly terms and coping well with other people.

clue.text: Study group combining business with pleasure

parts.note: doing business is being at work, working
a party is an occasion for pleasure

explanation.surface: A committee that mixes its work with a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee set up to investigate and report on a particular question.

clue.text: Commanding Officer in charge set about sergeant major — great!

indicators.note: the first two pieces together are placed around the next one, surrounding it

parts.note: CO is the standard military abbreviation for Commanding Officer

explanation.surface: An army officer attacks a sergeant major, and someone cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' reads as 'attacked', as if the officer were assaulting the sergeant major, but it is the container signal; 'great!' is the definition, a hippie-era exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for wonderful or terrific, as in 'that's cosmic, man'.

clue.text: Zero standard of wartime prison

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: The prison conditions in wartime were of zero standard.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: German camp for captured officers during World War Two, from Offizierslager.

clue.text: They remind me repeatedly not to change direction

indicators.note: said more than once, so the word me appears twice

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: change means rearrange the letters of not

parts.note: S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Keepsakes keep telling me not to alter my course in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NOT into NTO; 'repeatedly' doubles ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvenirs are objects kept to remind one of people or events.

clue.text: Match money playing dice

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of dice are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Gamblers stake equal cash on a game of dice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns DICE into CIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to correspond or agree exactly, as two things that match do.

clue.text: Excellent act worth an encore

parts.note: read as a fine stage performance, it is really a kind deed that, as the proverb says, deserves another

explanation.surface: A theatre critic praises a variety act that deserves a repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'one good turn deserves another' is behind 'worth an encore'; 'act' and 'turn' are also both stage performances.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpful kind deed done for someone, which by the proverb merits one in return.

clue.text: Students of the past

parts.note: not historians, but people who were once students at a school or college

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like history scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Students of the past' suggests historians; it means former students.
explanation.definitionFit: Former pupils or graduates of a particular school or university.

clue.text: Visitors are barred — it's badly contaminated

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the next word are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A notice explains that visitors are kept out because the place is badly contaminated.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign meaning entry is forbidden, which is what keeps visitors out.

clue.text: Golden retriever's mate

parts.note: not a dog's partner: the retriever is Jason of Greek myth, who fetched the Golden Fleece, and this is his wife

explanation.surface: A dog lover asks about the partner of their golden retriever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden retriever' looks like the dog breed; it is Jason, who retrieved the Golden Fleece with the help of the sorceress who became his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The sorceress of Greek myth who helped Jason win the Golden Fleece and married him.

clue.text: In love and caring fantastically — it's a sort of chemistry

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

indicators.note: fantastically means the letters of caring are arranged wildly

explanation.surface: Being in love and caring wonderfully is said to be a kind of chemistry between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' turns CARING into RGANIC. The surface's romantic 'chemistry' is really a branch of science.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic chemistry is the branch dealing with compounds not based on carbon.

clue.text: A worthy person, as yet lacking polish

definitions.text: A worthy person, as yet lacking polish

parts.words: A worthy person, as yet lacking polish
parts.note: a good-hearted person with unrefined manners, likened to an uncut precious stone

explanation.surface: A description of a decent but unsophisticated person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polish' works for both manners and the cutting of a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for someone kind and good underneath an unrefined exterior, like an uncut gem.

clue.text: Irritation anyone can cause

indicators.note: the letters are made to produce something new, so to cause signals rearrangement here

explanation.surface: A remark that anybody is capable of causing irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cause' makes a new arrangement out of ANYONE CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance is a feeling of mild anger, a synonym of irritation.

clue.text: Shared in a good round of golf?

definitions.meaning: took part in or had a portion of something
split in two words, it describes a round where the standard score was achieved

explanation.surface: Someone shared in a fine round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PAR TAKEN, the second reading describes a golfer who scored par, a good round; the question mark flags the made-up phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Partaken means participated in or shared, the past participle of partake.

clue.text: We are its ruin, so to speak

indicators.note: ruin means the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gloomy confession that we are the downfall of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' wrecks WE ARE ITS into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are used to signal that words are used figuratively or loosely.

clue.text: Son is against being involved in secret trysts

indicators.note: being involved means the letters are tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A son disapproves of being caught up in clandestine love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Assignations are secret arrangements to meet, especially between lovers.

clue.text: The French bishop's responsibility for a tenant

parts.note: les is a French word for the, in its plural form
a see is a bishop's diocese, the area under him

explanation.surface: A French bishop takes on the care of a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee is a person who holds a property under a lease, a tenant.

clue.text: A Spaniard is a Greek

parts.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman, so a Spaniard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a Spanish man is in fact Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis was a beautiful youth in Greek mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: The handsome youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth is a Greek figure.

clue.text: Retaliation in kind from tart, fit to burst

indicators.note: burst means the letters break apart and come together in a new order

explanation.surface: Revenge from a woman so angry she is about to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' breaks up TART FIT TO; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for paying someone back in the same way they treated you.

clue.text: Do lie about being past one's prime

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person who is past their best, matching the noun

indicators.note: about here means the letters of the preceding words are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone tells others to lie about their age now they are getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DO LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for an older person, or for anything old and well loved.

clue.text: Admit defeat and return

definitions.meaning: the return on an investment, the profit it produces

explanation.surface: Someone concedes and goes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' looks like a verb of going back, but it is the noun meaning profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender, and a yield is the return produced by an investment.

clue.text: Requires sound massages

indicators.note: sound means the word is said aloud and spelt as another

parts.note: requires means needs

explanation.surface: A healthy body needs good massages.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working muscles with the hands, as a massage does.

clue.text: Belonging to different unions but working together

parts.note: to be in a club is to belong to it

indicators.note: different means the letters of unions are made into another word

explanation.surface: Workers from separate trade unions nonetheless cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges UNIONS to UNISON.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for acting in agreement, from singing or sounding the same note together.

clue.text: Female relatives of a pawnbroker?

parts.note: a pawnbroker is jokingly called 'uncle', so his family are the daughters of his siblings

explanation.surface: A question about a moneylender's female kin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker; the question mark marks the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters of one's brother or sister are relatives of an uncle.

clue.text: Young bounders in form

parts.note: not lively young cads, but baby hares, which bound and live in a hollow called a form

explanation.surface: Youthful rogues on good form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounders' is old British slang for cads; here they are creatures that bound, and a hare's nest is a 'form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Young hares, which leap along and rest in a shallow nest called a form.
